intended_statement: The paper intends a bijective conversion between rank-pattern data \(r=(r_{ij})\) and Kostant multiplicity data \(m=(m_{ab})\). Informally, the cumulative direction has the form \[ r_{ij}=\sum_{a\le i\le j\le b} m_{ab}, \] and the inverse direction is a finite-difference formula for recovering the multiplicities \(m_{ab}\) from the ranks \(r_{ij}\). Boundary conventions supply zero terms outside the valid index range.
summary: Rank-pattern/Kostant bijection \(r_{ij}=\sum_{a\le i\le j\le b}m_{ab}\) and its finite-difference inverse.

intended_statement: For the fixed dimension vector \(\mathbf d\) of the equioriented type \(A\) quiver, let \(\mathbf m=(m_{kl})\in\mathcal M_{\mathbf d}^{+}\) be a Kostant partition and let \(\mathbf r=(r_{ij})\in\mathcal R_{\mathbf d}\) be the corresponding rank pattern, so that \(r_{ij}=\sum_{k\leq i\leq j\leq l}m_{kl}\). Then the \(G\)-orbit in \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(k)\) corresponding to \(\mathbf m\) is exactly \(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{rk}=\mathbf r}=\{(A_1,\ldots,A_N)\in\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}\mid \operatorname{rank}(A_j\cdots A_{i+1})=r_{ij}\text{ for all }0\leq i<j\leq N\}\). Equivalently, in this source passage the intended claim is that the interval multiplicities recover the ranks of all path-compositions by cumulative counting, and those rank conditions characterize the associated orbit.
summary: Proposition 3.1(b) identifies the orbit associated to a Kostant partition \(\mathbf m\) with the locus of representations whose composition ranks equal the corresponding rank pattern \(\mathbf r\); the rank entries are cumulative counts of interval summands.
